name: elm-safe-virtual-dom
description: A robust virtual DOM for Elm.

paragraphs: Can this be used in production? Yes! Here’s a little timeline: - May 2025: After a careful gradual rollout during May 2025, Insurello starts using this in production. With a couple of thousand unique users per day, there hasn’t been a single error reported automatically or to customer service. - June 2025: Multiple people on Discord start trying it out. They find a few bugs, which I never ran into at Insurello, but I manage to fix them quickly. - July 2025: Some more bugs are fixed. - September 2025: StorageMart starts using this in production. - November 2025: NoRedInk starts using this in…
features: Documents the changes I’ve made in forks of DOM related core Elm packages.
Documents how to use my forks in your own project.
Is where you can open issues for things specific to my forks.

requirements.text: If you do server-side rendering and expect Elm to hydrate/virtualize/adopt/take charge over the server-side rendered HTML, you need to make sure that all elements (except the root element) have data-elm.
